knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=3 t,\qquad y=t^{2} + 1,\qquad -2\le t\le 2.
$$

Fill in the three blanks in the table. Give exact values.

Use the value of $t$ at the top of each column in the formula for that row. For example, $x(-2)=3 \left(-2\right)=-6$.

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-6$ | $-3$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | {{field-2}} | $2$ | {{field-3}} |

| **$t$** | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $3$ | {{field-1}} |
| $y$ | $2$ | $5$ |
question.:question/worked-solution:
The missing entry is in the $x$-row under $t=2$. Substitute into $x=3 t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(2) &=3 \left(2\right) \\ &=6\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $y$-row under $t=-2$. Substitute into $y=t^{2} + 1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-2) &=\left(-2\right)^{2} + 1 \\ &=5\end{aligned}
$$

The missing entry is in the $y$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $y=t^{2} + 1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) &=\left(0\right)^{2} + 1 \\ &=1\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-6$ | $-3$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | $5$ | $2$ | $1$ |

| **$t$** | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $3$ | $6$ |
| $y$ | $2$ | $5$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}x(-2) &=\left(-2\right)^{2} - \left(-2\right) - 2 \\ &=4\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right),\qquad y=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right).
$$

Consider the following table of values. Angles are in radians.

| **$t$** | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $a$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $b$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $c$ | $-1$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

Find the exact value of $a+b+c$.

{{result}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The $a$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(0\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(0\right) \\ &=1\end{aligned}
$$

The $b$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=-1$. Substitute into $y=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}b &=\tan\left(\frac{\pi \left(-1\right)}{3}\right) \\ &=\tan\left(- \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The $c$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=3$. Substitute into $x=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(3\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \\ &=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+b+c &=\left(1\right)+\left(- \sqrt{3}\right)+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $-1$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right),\qquad y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right).
$$

Consider the following table of values. Angles are in radians.

| **$t$** | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $a$ | $-1$ | $b$ |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ |

| **$t$** | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $1$ | $c$ |

Find the exact value of $a-b+c$.

{{result}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The $a$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=-4$. Substitute into $x=\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a &=\sin\left(\frac{\pi \left(-4\right)}{6}\right) \\ &=\sin\left(- \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) \\ &=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The $b$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=-2$. Substitute into $x=\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}b &=\sin\left(\frac{\pi \left(-2\right)}{6}\right) \\ &=\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ &=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The $c$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=1$. Substitute into $y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(1\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}a-b+c &=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ |

The $c$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=-4$. Substitute into $y=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\tan\left(\frac{\pi \left(-4\right)}{3}\right) \\ &=\tan\left(- \frac{4 \pi}{3}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}-a+b+c &=-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\left(- \sqrt{3}\right)+\left(- \sqrt{3}\right) \\ &=- 2 \sqrt{3} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-1$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

| **$t$** | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $-1$ |
| $y$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |

knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right),\qquad y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right).
$$

Consider the following table of values. Angles are in radians.

| **$t$** | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $- \frac{1}{2}$ | $a$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $b$ | $1$ | $c$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $-1$ |

Find the exact value of $a+b+c$.

{{result}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The $a$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=0$. Substitute into $x=\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a &=\sin\left(\frac{\pi \left(0\right)}{6}\right) \\ &=\sin\left(0\right) \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

The $b$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=-1$. Substitute into $y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}b &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(-1\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(- \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The $c$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=1$. Substitute into $y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(1\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+b+c &=\left(0\right)+\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $- \frac{1}{2}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ |
| $y$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $-1$ |

knowledge_point.title: Filling a Table of Values for a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
Consider the curve with parametric equations

$$
x=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right),\qquad y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right).
$$

Consider the following table of values. Angles are in radians.

| **$t$** | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | $b$ |
| $y$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |
| $y$ | $c$ | $a$ |

Find the exact value of $-a+b-c$.

{{result}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The $a$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=4$. Substitute into $y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(4\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(\pi\right) \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The $b$ entry is in the $x$-row under $t=2$. Substitute into $x=\tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}b &=\tan\left(\frac{\pi \left(2\right)}{3}\right) \\ &=\tan\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The $c$ entry is in the $y$-row under $t=3$. Substitute into $y=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}c &=\cos\left(\frac{\pi \left(3\right)}{4}\right) \\ &=\cos\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \\ &=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the three entries with the signs in the requested expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}-a+b-c &=-\left(-1\right)+\left(- \sqrt{3}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=- \sqrt{3} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is

| **$t$** | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | $- \sqrt{3}$ |
| $y$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $0$ |

| **$t$** | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |
| $y$ | $- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ | $-1$ |
